GUIDEBOOK_CHAPTERS.title: Know Your California Lemon Law Rights
GUIDEBOOK_CHAPTERS.summary: Song-Beverly basics, warranty timing, and what substantial impairment means in plain English.
GUIDEBOOK_CHAPTERS.thumbnailAlt: California courthouse columns at golden hour

sections.title: What actually matters for a case
paragraphs: What we care about is whether the defect first occurred during the original manufacturer warranty. Manufacturers sometimes push an 18-month / 18,000-mile story online. That window is not required to have a case, and it does not decide whether you have a good case.
Repair history and days in the shop help show the manufacturer has not cured the problem.

sections.title: Substantial impairment in real life
paragraphs: Courts and manufacturers look at whether the defect affects how you use the car, what it is worth, or whether it is safe. Chronic stalling, brake issues, and repeat powertrain failures usually qualify. Minor rattles alone often do not.
Keep a simple log: date, mileage, symptom, and how it affected your commute or family plans.

sections.title: Who pays the attorney
paragraphs: Manufacturers always pay our attorney fees, or the representation is free. Clients of CLINE APC do not pay any fees, ever.

GUIDEBOOK_CHAPTERS.title: The Buyback & Settlement Process
GUIDEBOOK_CHAPTERS.summary: From repair records to manufacturer demand: how buybacks, replacements, and cash settlements work.

sections.title: Records that help a claim
paragraphs: Repair orders help if you have them. A purchase or lease contract is useful. We often take cases when the account is clear and believable even without a complete file.
The documentation checklist organizes records on hand. We do not need a window sticker.

sections.title: Mileage offset
paragraphs: Buybacks include a statutory usage deduction based on miles driven before the first repair for the defect. Our buyback calculator models the formula for a directional estimate.

sections.title: Buyback, replacement, or cash
paragraphs: Manufacturers may offer repurchase, a comparable replacement, or a negotiated cash settlement. The best path depends on your loan balance, how long you have been without a reliable vehicle, and whether the defect is safety-related.

GUIDEBOOK_CHAPTERS.title: Documentation That Wins Claims
GUIDEBOOK_CHAPTERS.summary: Repair orders, notices, and timelines that prove repeat defects and days out of service.
GUIDEBOOK_CHAPTERS.thumbnailAlt: Organized folder of automotive repair invoices

sections.title: Repair orders that tell the story
paragraphs: Each visit should capture your complaint, mileage in and out, dates in the shop, parts replaced, and diagnostic codes. Ask for copies before you leave the service drive.
“Could not duplicate” visits still matter when you have video or a pattern of return visits.

sections.title: Written notice to the manufacturer
paragraphs: Your warranty booklet usually explains how to notify the automaker. Certified mail and portal messages create a dated record that you gave the manufacturer a chance to cure the defect.

sections.title: A checklist for records on hand
paragraphs: The documentation checklist organizes repair orders, a contract, and other records you already have. We do not need a window sticker, and we do not need a complete packet to take your case.

GUIDEBOOK_CHAPTERS.title: Arbitration, Demands & Settlement
GUIDEBOOK_CHAPTERS.summary: How warranty arbitration fits with Song-Beverly court remedies and what happens after a demand letter.
GUIDEBOOK_CHAPTERS.thumbnailAlt: Conference table with legal files and pen

sections.title: Manufacturer arbitration programs
paragraphs: Many warranties reference state-certified arbitration (such as BBB AUTO LINE). Arbitration is not always mandatory before hiring counsel, but your warranty language matters.
Whether you arbitrate first or move directly to an attorney depends on your repair history and deadlines.

sections.title: Structured demands
paragraphs: A strong demand packages the warranty-period defect, repair history you have, and the requested remedy (buyback, replacement, or settlement). We build that file - you do not need to complete it before you call.

sections.title: Typical settlement timeline
paragraphs: Many matters resolve in a few months when records are clear. Litigation takes longer but remains available if the manufacturer refuses a fair remedy.

GUIDEBOOK_CHAPTERS.title: Deadlines & Statute of Limitations
GUIDEBOOK_CHAPTERS.summary: When the clock starts, why early action protects your records, and how four years usually applies.
GUIDEBOOK_CHAPTERS.thumbnailAlt: Calendar and car keys on a desk

sections.title: The four-year window
paragraphs: Song-Beverly claims generally must be filed within four years, but the start date can be earlier than owners expect, often when you knew or should have known about the defect and the failure to repair.

sections.title: Warranty timing vs. the filing deadline
paragraphs: Whether the defect first occurred during the original manufacturer warranty is a case question. The statute of limitations is a separate filing deadline. Do not assume an 18-month / 18,000-mile story ends your rights - call us.

sections.title: Why act while records are fresh
paragraphs: Dealers merge and service writers leave. Getting repair orders now is easier than reconstructing a timeline years later.
